chapter: Soprano sax and working with Bechet
title: Soprano saxophone and why Rose avoided saxophones
summary: Rose says he sees little place for soprano sax in an ensemble, considers solos an intermission, and never recorded saxophone after his first session.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: What do you think of a soprano sax as an instrument?

Well, I don't think there's much excuse for it actually. It is not bad as a solo instrument, although it's not as true as I like to hear an instrument. But of course there is no place for it in any kind of ensemble. And you know, the fact of the matter is that my own feeling about jazz, I really can't ever really get excited about solos. And to me, a solo or a vocal chorus is more or less an intermission. And it's not that I have anything against them, it's just that that's not the point where I'm listening. I'm always listening for that band sound. And I'd be very happy if you never heard a solo.
Well, a session like Doc and His Patience, you had soprano then, didn't you?
Yeah. There was some soprano, although in some cases they were playing two clarinets.
But you repressed the saxophone play. Oh yeah.

Other than that session, that first session that I made, I never again recorded a saxophone. And any session that I was personally in control of, in charge of, I never used a saxophone. And only on certain occasions did I use saxophones in concerts, and they were for special purposes. Like for example, Bud Freeman worked a couple of sessions for me. But that had a lot to do with the politics of the band, rather than my own musical preference.
